about: Settings for the Graded Heat bot (scripts/graded_heat.py). Edit and commit to change what it watches. Nothing here touches the cards on the site.
max_slab_price_about: The most you'd pay for one slab (PSA 10 or PSA 9). All three slab bots skip slabs over this in both grades (no requests spent on them) and the Graded Slabs tab only lists slabs with a PSA 10 or PSA 9 at or under it. Change the number and commit; the next morning's runs use it. CardPrice still re-checks over-cap slabs every cp_over_cap_recheck_days days so ones that drop back under come back.
focus_about: The eras every slab bot looks at first and ranks a little higher (mid-era: DP/HGSS, Black & White, XY, Sun & Moon, 2007-2019). focus_priority_bonus: how far ahead they go in the check queues; focus_sort_bonus: heat points added when sorting the Graded Slabs list. Change the list (era ids from eras/eras.json) and commit.
est_about: For slabs only CardPrice has priced (an estimate, no sales behind it): its 4-week rise must be at least est_breaking_pct to show as Breaking out (estimates wobble 10-20% on their own), and a rise of est_glitch_pct or more is treated as a likely data glitch (Verify price).

sources.about: How the slab bots share work (graded/sources.json) and how the price to believe is picked (scripts/slab_sources.py). skip_if_other_checked_days: the eBay-sales bots (PokemonPriceTracker, pokemon-api.com) skip a slab the other checked this recently (heating-up slabs excepted). disagree_pct: sources within this % count as agreeing (confirmed). split_pct: two sources further apart than this can't be reconciled (price marked unverified). outlier_pct: with 3+ sources, one this far from the middle is thrown out. raw_bounds: plausible slab price vs the raw NM price [lowest multiple, highest multiple, $ slack]; anything outside is a wrong card or junk sale. max_psa10_to_psa9_ratio: a bigger gap than this marks the less certain grade unverified. weights: how much each source counts. psa9_share_of_psa10_guess: when only the PSA 10 price is known, guess the PSA 9 at this share of it for the cap test. price_fresh_days: prices older than this aren't used.

cp_about: CardPrice.com (scripts/cardprice_bot.py): free open API, 600 requests/min. ~2 requests per slab, so 400 slabs is ~800 a day (the whole pool about every 4 days).
pa_about: pokemon-api.com via RapidAPI (scripts/pokemon_api_bot.py, secret POKEMON_API_KEY). Free Basic plan: 100 requests a DAY, 30 a minute; requests over 100 are billed ($0.005 each). The bot stops at pa_max_per_day (90) and also when RapidAPI says only pa_keep_free (5) are left, so it stays inside the free 100.
priority_about: Your Pokémon, most important first. Slabs of these that are on the verge show first; other popular Pokémon (the 'popular' list in discovery_config.json) come after. The bot also checks these first.
